Present value of an annuity-certain

Source: R/4_financialFunctions.R
annuity.Rd

Compute the present value of a stream of fixed payments separated by equal intervals of time. Returns the perpetuity value when n = Inf.

Usage

annuity(i, n, m = 0, k = 1, type = "immediate")

Arguments

i

Effective interest rate expressed in decimal form (e.g. 0.03 for 3%). May also be a vector of per-period rates with the same length as the implied payment schedule.

n

Number of payment periods. Inf returns the value of a perpetuity (either immediate or due, depending on type).

m

Deferment period. Default 0.

k

Number of payments per year. A payment of \(1/k\) is assumed in each sub-period, so that the total yearly outflow stays equal to 1.

type

Payment timing. "immediate" (default) pays at the end of each period; "due" pays at the beginning. "arrears" and "advance" are the respective aliases (can be abbreviated).

Value

A numeric scalar: the present value of the annuity.

Details

For an annuity-immediate the first payment occurs at time \(1/k\); for an annuity-due the first payment occurs at time \(0\). The present value is obtained by delegating to presentValue with the appropriate payment schedule rather than closed-form formulas, which keeps the output consistent across other APV functions that reuse the same kernel.

Note

The value returned derives from direct discounting of the cash flow schedule, not from closed-form formulas such as \(a^{(m)}_{\overline{n}|} = (1 - v^n)/i^{(m)}\). When m > 1, the per-period payment is \(1/m\).

References

Broverman, S.A. (2008). Mathematics of Investment and Credit (Fourth Edition), ACTEX Publications.

See also

accumulatedValue, increasingAnnuity, decreasingAnnuity

Author

Giorgio A. Spedicato

Examples

# Present value of 1 per year, paid in arrears, for 10 years at 3%:
annuity(i = 0.03, n = 10)
#> [1] 8.530203
# Same but paid monthly (1/12 at the end of each month):
annuity(i = 0.03, n = 10, k = 12)
#> [1] 8.646867
# Perpetuity due:
annuity(i = 0.05, n = Inf, type = "due")
#> [1] 21
